recipes.name: Greek Chicken Pasta
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast meat - cut into bite-size pieces
1 (14 ounce) can marinated artichoke hearts, drained and chopped

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook pasta in boiling water until tender yet firm to the bit, 8 to 10 minutes; drain.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion and garlic; saute until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Stir in the chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 5 to 6 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium-low; add artichoke hearts, tomato, feta cheese, parsley, lemon juice, oregano, and cooked pasta. Cook and stir until heated through, about 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat, season with salt and pepper, and garnish with lemon wedges.

raw_recipe.headline: Greek Chicken Pasta
raw_recipe.description: For a fabulously flavorful dish that takes just minutes to make, simply saute garlic, onion and tender strips of chicken. Add artichoke hearts, tomato, feta cheese, parsley, lemon juice and oregano, and toss with hot pasta.

video.description: A simple Greek chicken pasta dish starring so many of the bright flavors of Greece-marinated artichoke hearts, tomatoes, feta cheese, and oregano.

review.reviewBody: DELICIOUS! WOW, what a great tasting pasta dish. I added just a touch of butter with the olive oil to cook the onions (adds some great flavour), seasoned the chicken breasts with salt and pepper before cooking, used half of the oregano suggested (not a huge fan) and used whole wheat penne pasta. I used reduced fat feta cheese which melted right away and created this beautiful, light, creamy sauce. Everyone that tried it absolutely LOVED it. I'm so thrilled that I found this recipe. I will be using this for many years to come. DEVINE recipe Lalena... thank you so much for posting!

Easy, quick and delicious! I made a half batch. Didn’t have a tomato, so subbed chopped, roasted peppers. Subbed butter for olive oil. Took juice from artichokes and roasted peppers, added lemon juice, 1 Tbsp butter, oregano, 2 tsp cornstarch a half tsp chicken bouillion and some tomato sauce. Cooked over medium heat till thickened and set thickened sauce aside. Cooked thinly sliced chicken breast with butter, onion and garlic in electric skillet, adding the cooked pasta and sauce. Threw in some grated parmesan, and served with crumbled feta sauce on top. It was very flavorful and so quick and easy to make. I will definitely make it again, as it’s a fun recipe that is easily modified based on personal preference and/or what you have on-hand. Two thumbs up

This was so incredibly good, I signed up just so I could leave a review (and I’ve been using this site for years without signing up). The flavor was incredible, and my kids loved it as well, and cleared their plates, despite being picky eaters. Here are the modifications I made. I didn’t drain the artichokes in order to make the pasta more moist, I used only about 2/3 the amount of pasta it said to use. I used rigate pasta rather than linguine, I added a handful of kalamata olives, some Italian marinated grilled mushrooms, a drizzle of olive oil and butter when it was almost done cooking (for added moisture), a sprinkle of parmesan cheese, and a dash of garlic powder. I omitted the parsley, salt, and pepper. It was so good I cannot wait to cook it again. Best recipe I’ve ever gotten from this site.

This was incredible! Lots of flavor, lots of color. As most users, I tweaked this recipe a bit. I used less than half the amount of pasta. I added a bit of butter to the olive oil (used twice the amount of olive oil), onion and garlic. I used double the amount of garlic. I used marinated chicken (bought from the grocery store, Italian marinade). After cooking the chicken, I added the rest of the ingredients listed above. I added spinach, kale, and chard to the mix for some added color and nutrients. I let everything simmer for 10-15 minutes to let everything combine. I didn't add the pasta into the skillet, I instead spooned the chicken mixture over the penne pasta with the juice. 

A really light, yet filling meal. The flavors were unbelievable! The sauce was perfect. Not too tangy/acidic with the lemon, and not too creamy with the feta. Just the right amount. I loved the added benefit of the spinach/kale/chard to the mix, added a great color to everything. The olives were a needed bonus as well, absolutely delicious!

Delicious! As noted by others, I added the kalamata olives; my personal taste required doubling the garlic. I had 3 cups of diced rotisserie chicken to be used up, so added that when I added the pasta (rigatoni) instead of sauteing as directed. As someone else mentioned, this could also be a side dish without the chicken as mine was very flavorful.

Delicious!! So easy to make I will definitely make again, it would be great for a dinner party. I did add 1/3 cup chopped Kalamata olives and I had 8 asparagus spears I chopped up into 1" pieces and sauteed with the onions and garlic.

As written 4 stars!! To make it a 5 star in our house I marinated the chicken in the drained juice from the artichoke hearts for a little while before cooking and used 8oz of Penne vs 16oz Linguine, Great dish and will make again!!!

This is sooo good! I've made it so many times and I'm pretty sure it's my new favorite food. I buy a big package of chicken thighs/breasts and bake and shred it beforehand, separate it out into little baggies and throw them in the freezer. Then I can just grab a bag out when I'm ready to make this. It makes it so fast and easy! Make sure to use the marinated artichokes in the jar, not the cheaper canned ones... I've found they have a lot of tough/chewy pieces. I use a can of diced italian tomatoes (not drained), and plenty of feta. I usually add in a little juice from the artichokes and a little from the kalamata olives. I also use the "Garden Delight" pasta spirals. I prefer to eat this hot, but is delicious cold as well!

I only gave this 4 stars as based on other recommendations- briefly marinated chicken in artichoke oil, added a tsp plu a bit of butter, added red and yellow peppers, doubled the garlic. We really liked it and will make it again. I think it would also be really good with capers.

I was searching this site for a Greek inspired chicken dish. I had most of the ingredients on hand, made a few tiny tweaks and it was superb!! I subbed a vidallia onion b/c it's what I had on hand, used a drained can of petite diced tomatoes, again, i didn't have a fresh one on hand. I added 1/3 cup of sliced Kalamata olives and added the marinade from the artichokes back in at the end and simmered the dish with all ingredients including the feta, which melted to a yummy consistency. I used a 12 oz box of campanelli - I didn't have the linguini. (I do think the 12 oz box is as large as you should go, or the pasta would be too dry.) Tossed all together before serving and sprinkled a little more feta on top. Hubby & kids all had seconds?? I'm adding this to the rotation!!!

This has become our favorite pasta meal for the two of us. The lemon highlights the artichokes and the oregano and parsley are perfect spices! I made some adjustments for our tastes and to serve two. I cook 4 oz dry whole wheat spaghetti for the two of us. I use one four-ounce chicken breast cut into bite-sized pieces; half of a 33.5 ounce jar of artichokes (drained), quartered rather than chopped; 14.5 oz canned diced tomatoes, undrained, in place of a large chopped tomato. I add 1/4 teaspoon of red crushed pepper; 3.8 oz sliced black olives, drained; 1 teaspoon sugar. I don't add the pasta or feta cheese to the sauce. I put the cooked pasta in a bowl and pour sauce over it, then top each serving with feta cheese. I add a tossed salad and we have a satisfying, wonderful tasty meal! Thank you, Lalena!
Not enough juice for sauce

OMG!! This is amazing. Everyone should try this if you have even a tiny bit of love for the ingredients. I reserved the marinade from the Artichoke jar based on some of the reviews but I didn't need any of it. This recipe was perfect as written.
I need more liquid because I used gluten free linguine but I will make it again.
Was very good. I I used cavitappi pasta for fun presentation. Also added white wine and Kalamata olives when adding the other veggies. Delicious.
I loved this and my picky kids even loved it. Hubby enjoyed it, too. I eliminated the dairy but it tasted so yummy! I can’t wait to make this again.

I used canned petite tomatoes as someone suggested (I didn't have fresh ones) and included the juice. It tasted very good, but was mushier than I expected. I will definitely make it again. My husband loved it.

This was very good and a nice mix of flavors. I pretty much followed the recipe as written. I used penne instead of linguini and seasoned the chicken with Lawry's low sodium seasoning salt. I also used most of the liquid from the artichokes for more flavor and to prevent the pasta from being too dry as suggested by other reviews. Will definitely make again. Thanks for the recipe.
Amazing recipe! I would double the amount of feta and didn't add the olives (I have a family member who won't eat them) but otherwise it was very good
My wife and daughter love this dish, made according to the recipe,keeper
